experiment: M4: ridge alpha grid + holdout selection criterion (WS-M)
spec: gate pre-registered in docs/prelaunch-2026-07/GATES.md section M4

method.baseline: shipped ridge: alphas [1.0, 10.0, 100.0], holdout min weighted MAE
method.treatment: alphas [0.3, 1.0, 3.0, 10.0, 30.0, 100.0, 300.0], holdout MAX weighted Spearman (KM weights retained, same seeded permutation holdout)
method.eval: forward-chained eFV blend, debuted target_censored, test>=15/train>=60, blend at live lambda -- identical to rank_calibration
method.note: efv_model imports prospect_path._fit_ridge, so this ridge config feeds the shipped eFV blend directly.

loss_ledger.summary: Widening the alpha grid and switching the holdout criterion to weighted Spearman did not clear the M4 gate; prospect_path._ALPHAS and the MAE selection criterion are retained unchanged.
loss_ledger.asymmetry: The change HELPS pit (blend rho +0.0121, within-tier +0.0208, t45 +0.0267) but badly HURTS hit (-0.0165, within-tier -0.0486, t45 -0.0225). The weighted-Spearman criterion pins alpha at the grid max (300) every fold for hitters -- over-regularizing the ridge collapses it toward the FV prior and kills the within-tier signal that is eFV's value-add. Fails c2 (hit -0.0165 < -0.002), c3 (hit tier), c4 (hit 2022-2023 -0.0204).
loss_ledger.keep_alive: grid_vs_criterion_diagnostic disentangles it: pit's gain is CRITERION-driven, not grid-driven (base_grid+wspearman pit 0.2757 -> 0.2839 = +0.0082; wide_grid+MAE pit -0.0030). The WIDE grid is what poisons hitters -- it lets weighted-Spearman reach alpha 300 (base_grid+wspearman hit is a near-neutral -0.0006, wide_grid+wspearman hit is -0.0165). So the promising future cell is weighted-Spearman selection ON THE BASE GRID (pit +0.0082, hit ~neutral), NOT the wide grid. That is a DIAGNOSTIC observation only -- the pre-registered M4 change bundled wide grid + criterion and that bundle fails; carving out base_grid+wspearman post-hoc would be goalpost-moving. Re-open it as its own pre-registered gate (criterion-only, base grid, per-side alpha cap).
